stories.headline: Police rescue abandoned dog in Newton-in-the-Isle
stories.brief:
The Rural Crime Action Team has rescued a large dog found abandoned in a small cage near a road in Newton-in-the-Isle. Officers attended the scene following a report from a member of the public. 

A police spokesperson thanked the individual who alerted them to the animal’s condition, allowing officers to remove the dog from the cage and the roadside. An investigation into the incident is currently underway.

stories.headline: West Norfolk Council advances plans for new £22.9m aquatic centre
stories.brief:
West Norfolk Council has voted to progress plans for a new £22.9 million aquatic centre at Lynnsport in King’s Lynn. The proposed facility would feature an eight-lane main pool, a learner pool with a moveable floor, and an interactive splash pad. 

Officials say the current St James Swimming Pool has reached the end of its economic life. The council has approved over £845,000 to fund the next two stages of design and technical planning. While this move advances the project, the council noted that this does not commit them to final construction. Officers estimate a planning application could be submitted by March 2027, with the project aiming to improve accessibility for residents across the region.

stories.headline: Pedestrian hospitalised following collision in March
stories.brief:
A pedestrian has been taken to Peterborough City Hospital following a collision with a car in March this morning. Emergency services were called to Wisbech Road at 8:55 am. 

The pedestrian sustained minor injuries and was taken to the hospital as a precaution. Wisbech Road was temporarily closed while emergency crews attended the scene.

stories.headline: West Norfolk students explore local manufacturing careers
stories.brief:
One hundred and fifty students from across West Norfolk have taken part in behind-the-scenes tours of seven major local businesses. The visits, held yesterday to mark National Manufacturing Day, allowed pupils from schools, colleges and the Boost programme to meet industry professionals and learn about diverse career paths.

Participating firms included Mars, Ravago, and Williams Refrigeration. The event, supported by the borough council, highlighted the importance of the manufacturing sector, which contributes over 500 million pounds to the local economy. Students explored various roles ranging from engineering and logistics to food production, gaining insight into opportunities available through apprenticeships and degree-level study.

stories.headline: Cambridgeshire sex offender sentenced for 1990s crimes
stories.brief: A Cambridgeshire man has been jailed following a cold case investigation into sexual assaults dating back to the 1990s. The offender was identified after modern DNA analysis linked him to the historical crimes. The case was reported by The Hunts Post.

stories.headline: Peterborough City Council considers opening a new children's home
stories.brief: Peterborough City Council is exploring plans to establish its own children's home. The local authority is currently looking into the possibility of opening the facility to support its social care services. No further details regarding the location or timeline for the project have been released at this stage.

stories.headline: East Cambridgeshire homeowners reduce property prices to secure sales
stories.brief: Homeowners across East Cambridgeshire are lowering their asking prices by thousands of pounds in an effort to finalise property sales. According to reports from the Ely Standard, sellers are adjusting their expectations to help secure deals in the current market. Residents looking to move or purchase a home in the region may find these price reductions impacting local listings.

stories.headline: Police attend supermarket roof collapse in Cambridgeshire
stories.brief: Emergency services have been called to a supermarket in Cambridgeshire following the collapse of its roof. Police are currently on the scene at the site. No further details regarding the location of the store or any potential injuries have been released at this time. Residents are advised to avoid the immediate area while authorities manage the situation.

stories.headline: Forget-Me-Not Luncheon Club marks 60th anniversary
stories.brief:
The Forget-Me-Not Luncheon Club in Gaywood is celebrating six decades of community service. To mark the milestone, a special two-course lunch is being held at the Gaywood Church Rooms on October 14 at noon. The event will include tea and coffee, with tickets priced at £10.

Organisers are inviting members of the community to attend the celebration. Anyone wishing to join must book their place by October 7 by calling 07715 400199 and leaving a message. The club, which provides companionship for senior residents, typically meets on Wednesdays during term time.

stories.headline: Arrest made following police call-out in Cambridgeshire
stories.brief: Police have made an arrest on suspicion of actual bodily harm following a report concerning a person's welfare. Officers were called to the scene to investigate the situation. The individual remains in custody while enquiries continue. No further details regarding the location or the identity of those involved have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Looking back at West Norfolk headlines from the archives
stories.brief:
This week we look back at local news from late September 1961. Among the stories reported at the time, a 17-year-old farmworker from Sedgeford was fined one pound by Docking magistrates for cycling without due care and attention following a collision in Heacham. 

Elsewhere in the region, Lynn Town Council discussed plans for a new cattle market and potential town expansion. Meanwhile, in 1986, comedian Norman Collier brought the cast of Hunstanton’s summer show to the King’s Lynn town hall for a reception with the Mayor. The theatre production had enjoyed a successful nine-week run at the Princess Theatre, prompting organisers to arrange free return coach travel for local theatre-goers.

stories.headline: Match officials confirmed for Peterborough United versus Stockport County
stories.brief: The match officials have been announced for the upcoming fixture between Peterborough United and Stockport County. The game, which will see Peterborough United playing at home, is set to go ahead as scheduled. Fans planning to attend the match at the Weston Homes Stadium should be aware that the officiating team has now been appointed for the encounter.

stories.headline: Winners announced for Cambridgeshire Make a Difference awards
stories.brief: The recipients of this year's Make a Difference awards in Cambridgeshire have been officially revealed. The annual honours, organised by the BBC, celebrate individuals who have made a positive impact within their local communities. While the names of the successful nominees have now been made public, further details regarding the specific categories and the individuals honoured are available through the BBC’s coverage of the event.

stories.headline: Improvement plan drafted for school facing termination notice
stories.brief: A school has developed a formal improvement plan following the receipt of a Termination Warning Notice. The document has been drawn up to demonstrate that the institution is capable of making the necessary progress required by authorities. Further details regarding the specific school involved or the timeline for these improvements have not been disclosed.

stories.headline: Investigation launched following alleged assault at Cambridgeshire school
stories.brief: An investigation is underway following reports that a boy was assaulted at a school in Cambridgeshire. Details regarding the specific location of the incident or the condition of the child involved have not yet been released. Authorities are currently looking into the circumstances surrounding the alleged event.

stories.headline: Climate-themed theatre production comes to Wisbech
stories.brief: A new production titled ‘A Just Transition: Jobs, People, Planet’ is coming to Wisbech this autumn. The Banner Theatre performance explores the shift toward a climate-friendly economy through live music, songs, and interviews. The show will be staged at St Peter's Church Hall on Saturday, October 10. Doors open at 3pm for stalls and refreshments, with the performance beginning at 4pm. Admission is free, supported by the TUC and local Trades Union Councils. Organisers advise booking tickets in advance due to limited space. You can secure a seat by emailing wmdtuc@gmail.com.

stories.headline: Inquest concludes into death of retired King’s Lynn police officer
stories.brief:
An inquest at Norfolk Coroner’s Court has ruled that 65-year-old Patrick Kavanagh died from a rare complication following a heart valve replacement. Mr Kavanagh, a retired police officer from Gaywood, was admitted to the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in June last year suffering from chest pains and breathing difficulties. Despite receiving treatment, he suffered a cardiac arrest and passed away on July 1. 

Area coroner Maeve Sykes concluded that the hospital provided appropriate care, noting that the death resulted from a rare mechanical valve dysfunction. The Queen Elizabeth Hospital trust has expressed its condolences to the family, confirming it had no concerns regarding the medical treatment provided to Mr Kavanagh.

stories.headline: Burglary reported at family-run tattoo studio in the Fens
stories.brief: Police are investigating a burglary at a family-run tattoo studio located in a Fenland town. Details regarding the exact location and the timing of the incident have not been released, but authorities are currently looking into the break-in. Anyone with information that could assist with the ongoing enquiries is encouraged to contact the police.

stories.headline: Motorcyclist seriously injured in King’s Lynn collision
stories.brief:
A motorcyclist has been taken to hospital with serious injuries following a collision with a car in King’s Lynn this morning. Emergency services were called to the Southgates roundabout at 6:22am. 

The driver of the car, a man in his 40s, was arrested on suspicion of driving while disqualified. He remains in custody at the King’s Lynn Police Investigation Centre for questioning. The scene of the collision was cleared by 8am.

stories.headline: Wisbech charity appeals for mannequin donations
stories.brief:
The Salvation Army Donation Centre on Cromwell Road in Wisbech is asking for help from the public. Staff are currently looking for spare mannequins to assist with upcoming Christmas displays at the shop. Anyone who has a mannequin they no longer need is encouraged to bring it to the centre. 

The charity says these figures are essential for showcasing items effectively as they prepare for the festive season. For further information or to get in touch with the team, you can visit their website at salvationarmytrading.org.uk/location/wisbech/.

stories.headline: North Lynn man to face court over building site burglaries
stories.brief:
A 37-year-old man from North Lynn is due to appear at Norwich Crown Court next month to face charges related to building site burglaries in West Norfolk. Arunas Abartis, of Lady Jane Grey Road, has been charged with three counts of trespass and four counts of stealing diesel from sites in South Wootton, Hunstanton, Downham, and King’s Lynn. 

The charges follow an arrest made by Norfolk Police on the evening of Monday, September 21. Mr Abartis has been bailed until his court appearance on October 21. Officers also conducted a search at a property on Lynn Road in Terrington St Clement earlier this week, though the police cordon at that location has now been removed.

stories.headline: New podiatry clinic opens in West Lynn
stories.brief:
A new specialist foot care clinic has opened its doors at the East Coast Business Park in West Lynn. Located at Unit 15, CH Podiatry is led by clinical director Chioma Harris, who brings experience from both the NHS and private practice. She is joined by foot health practitioner Donna Barr.

The clinic offers professional assessments and treatments for a variety of conditions, including heel pain, nail issues, corns, and calluses. The team is also focusing on nail surgery for ingrowing toenails and verrucae needling. The practice is now welcoming patients of all ages for both routine and preventative foot care.

stories.headline: Funding boost to tackle rough sleeping in Cambridgeshire and Peterborough
stories.brief: A new funding package worth one point seven five million pounds has been announced to help address rough sleeping across Cambridgeshire and Peterborough. The investment aims to support efforts to reduce homelessness in the region. Further details on how the money will be allocated are expected to follow as local authorities work to implement the new measures.

stories.headline: Career change for former roofer at HMP Whitemoor
stories.brief: A former roofer has begun a new career at HMP Whitemoor. The news was reported by the March Chatteris Whittlesey News. No further details regarding the individual or the nature of the role have been released.

stories.headline: New road markings installed at Gaywood clock junction
stories.brief:
New cross-hatching has been painted at the Gaywood clock junction to help improve traffic flow. The markings are designed to prevent vehicles queuing from Wootton Road from blocking the junction, which previously restricted traffic travelling from Gayton Road. 

Gaywood councillor Rob Colwell, who secured funding for the project through his Local Member Fund, said the change aims to ensure emergency service vehicles can pass through the area more easily. The work follows concerns raised by local residents and consultations with emergency services regarding congestion at the site. Councillor Colwell pursued the installation with Norfolk County Council following delays to road-lining schemes across the region.

stories.headline: Cambridgeshire MPs express frustration over council reorganisation delays
stories.brief: Members of Parliament representing Cambridgeshire have voiced their anger regarding ongoing delays to the planned reorganisation of local councils. The concerns follow reports that the restructuring process has not progressed as expected. No further details regarding the specific nature of the delays or the proposed changes have been provided at this time.

stories.headline: MP raises concerns over Whittlesey fish deaths in Parliament
stories.brief: The Member of Parliament for the area has formally raised the issue of recent fish deaths in Whittlesey during a session in Parliament. The matter was brought to the attention of the House following reports of the incident. No further details regarding the cause of the deaths or the specific location have been provided at this stage.

stories.headline: Final week for West Norfolk development consultation
stories.brief:
Residents in West Norfolk have until midnight on Monday, September 29, to share their views on the borough’s future Local Plan. The council is seeking public feedback on where new housing, schools, jobs, and transport links should be located. 

While landowners have suggested various sites for potential development, the council confirms that no final selections have been made. Officials are particularly encouraging young people and those experiencing poverty to participate in the process. You can submit your comments online or collect a paper form from the reception at Kings Court on Chapel Street in King's Lynn. This consultation is an early step in the planning process, with a draft version of the plan expected to undergo further public review next year.

stories.headline: Peterborough council leader calls for councillor to resign
stories.brief: The leader of Peterborough City Council has publicly requested the resignation of a local councillor following a drink-driving conviction. The call comes after reports confirmed the member’s involvement in the offence. No further details regarding the councillor's identity or the specific circumstances of the incident have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Police investigation underway in Fenland town
stories.brief: Police have launched an investigation following the discovery of a woman’s body at a property in a Fenland town. Officers were called to the scene, though no further details regarding the location or the circumstances of the death have been released at this time. Authorities are currently working to establish the facts surrounding the incident. We will bring you more information as it becomes available.

stories.headline: Wisbech students raise funds for hedgehog rescue
stories.brief:
Three construction students from the College of West Anglia’s Wisbech campus have raised £294 for Ryston Rachel’s Hedgehog Hotel. Finn McAuley, Marc Watson and Erikas Rimkus created hedgehog houses using recycled materials, including old pallets and plastic bottles, as part of a WorldSkills project. 

The initiative combined practical construction skills with a focus on sustainability and wildlife support. The rescue centre has reported high demand for the student-made houses, which have helped raise both funds and awareness for the local hedgehog population. College staff have praised the students for their teamwork and for applying their professional skills to benefit the community.

stories.headline: New book explores the unusual history of King’s Lynn
stories.brief: A new book titled Quirky King’s Lynn has been released, detailing the town’s eccentric past. Author Bill Lovelock explores various legends, buildings, and characters, including tales of pirates, exorcists, and a mysterious fiddler. Mr. Lovelock, who previously wrote about Lowestoft, conducted his research by walking the streets of the town to uncover hidden details. The book highlights the town’s evolution from a major medieval port to a centre for industries like glassmaking and food canning. One notable feature is the story of the Wandering Piper, which links a local legend to the discovery of human and canine remains during road works in the 1930s. The book is now available for those interested in the area's history.

stories.headline: Mary, Queen of Scots exhibition opens at Peterborough Cathedral
stories.brief: A new exhibition dedicated to Mary, Queen of Scots has opened at Peterborough Cathedral. The display, which is supported by the Association of English Cathedrals, is now available for visitors to view at the site. Those interested in local history can find further details regarding the exhibition by visiting the cathedral’s official channels.

stories.headline: Former greyhound kennels and bungalow listed for sale
stories.brief: A property featuring a unique bungalow and former greyhound kennels has been placed on the market. The site is currently listed with an asking price of £315,000.

stories.headline: King’s Lynn Community Cinema Club announces three October screenings
stories.brief: The King’s Lynn Community Cinema Club has announced a series of three film events taking place at the Majestic next month. The schedule begins on Thursday, October 1, with a screening of Power Station, followed by a Q&A session and supper at the GroundWork Gallery. On Saturday, October 3, the club will host a costumed sing-along of Chitty Chitty Bang Bang in partnership with the Steampunk Society. Finally, the Steven Soderbergh film The Christophers will be shown on Thursday, October 8. Tickets are available through the Majestic, with discounts for club members. Non-members aged 18 and over are also welcome to attend, with entry priced at £6 cash on the door.

stories.headline: Ronnie Harvey scores from 50 yards in Peterborough match
stories.brief: Peterborough’s match against Colchester saw a remarkable goal from Ronnie Harvey. The player successfully found the net from 50 yards out during the fixture. The event was reported by Sky Sports.

stories.headline: Government funding awarded to tackle rough sleeping in Cambridgeshire
stories.brief:
Local authorities across Cambridgeshire and Peterborough have been awarded new government funding to help address rough sleeping in the region. The grants were confirmed following a recent announcement regarding national support for homelessness initiatives. 

The funding is intended to assist councils in their ongoing efforts to support those without permanent accommodation. Further details on how the individual local authorities plan to allocate these resources are expected to be released in due course. Residents are encouraged to check their local council websites for updates on how these measures may impact services in their specific area.

stories.headline: Spalding recycling firm seeks permission to remain at current site
stories.brief: A recycling business based in Spalding has submitted an application to continue operating from its existing location. The proposal, reported by the Spalding South Holland News, seeks formal permission for the firm to remain at its current site. No further details regarding the application or a potential decision date have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Inquest hears of fatal collision involving pothole
stories.brief: An inquest has been told that a young girl has died following a road traffic collision. The hearing was informed that the vehicle involved was travelling at speed when it struck a pothole. No further details regarding the location or the identity of those involved have been released at this stage.

stories.headline: Police seize vehicle and report driver in Wisbech
stories.brief: Police in Wisbech have seized a car and reported a driver following a stop on Norwich Road. Officers on the night shift pulled the vehicle over after detecting a strong smell of cannabis. During a search of the occupants, a 38-year-old man was arrested on suspicion of multiple offences, including the possession of cannabis. The vehicle has since been recovered by police.

stories.headline: North Lynn man charged following West Norfolk building site burglaries
stories.brief:
A 37-year-old man from North Lynn is due to appear at Norwich Magistrates’ Court today. Arunas Abartis, of Lady Jane Grey Road, faces charges relating to a series of building site burglaries across West Norfolk. He is accused of three counts of trespass at locations in South Wootton, Hunstanton, and Downham, alongside four counts of diesel theft in South Wootton, King’s Lynn, and Hunstanton.

Police arrested the man on the evening of Monday, September 21. Officers remain at a property on Lynn Road in Terrington St Clement, where a cordon is currently in place as part of the ongoing investigation.

stories.headline: New children's home approved in Lincolnshire
stories.brief: Planning permission has been granted for a new children's home in the region. The facility is intended to help address an urgent need for local residential care placements. The approval follows reports from the Spalding South Holland News regarding the project's development. No further details regarding the specific location or opening date have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Concerns raised over local services and community impact in West Norfolk
stories.brief:
Residents in West Norfolk have raised concerns regarding the future of local services, including the potential impact of school closures on village life and the future of the A&E unit at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital. Correspondents expressed worry that centralising services could affect community cohesion and emergency response times.

Separately, criticism has been directed at Royal Mail over recent service changes, including delivery schedules and collection times. Meanwhile, wildlife enthusiasts have celebrated the presence of 19 species of raptors and owls in the Snettisham area, crediting local conservation efforts. However, some contributors warned that ongoing residential development continues to pose a threat to local green habitats and wildlife.

stories.headline: Peterborough and Colchester football match update
stories.brief: A football match took place between Peterborough and Colchester on the 22nd of September, 2026. Details regarding the final score of the fixture have been reported by ESPN.

stories.headline: Cambridgeshire man sentenced for racist messages to footballer
stories.brief: A man from Cambridgeshire has been sentenced after sending racist messages to England footballer Djed Spence. The abuse was directed at the player via the social media platform X.

stories.headline: Family-run cafe reports successful start in Spalding
stories.brief: A family-operated cafe in Spalding is celebrating a successful opening period. According to reports from the Spalding South Holland News, the new business has performed well since launching. The owners have described the initial response from the local community as brilliant.

stories.headline: North West Norfolk MP visits King’s Lynn rental firm
stories.brief:
North West Norfolk MP James Wild has visited the Enterprise Rental Services branch in King’s Lynn to discuss the company’s local operations. During the visit, Mr Wild met with regional manager Alexander Knight to learn about the firm’s recruitment practices and its ongoing business growth.

The discussion also focused on the challenges of expanding an electric vehicle fleet. The company highlighted that securing the necessary funding and permissions for charging infrastructure at their premises remains a significant barrier. Mr Wild noted that the transition to electric vehicles requires the right support and infrastructure to ensure businesses can successfully manage the shift alongside consumers.

stories.headline: Cambridgeshire teenagers reach BAFTA gaming award finals
stories.brief: Young people from Cambridgeshire have been named as finalists in the latest BAFTA gaming awards. The prestigious competition recognises talent in the video game industry, with local teenagers securing their place among the final contenders. Further details regarding the specific projects or the identities of the nominees have not been released at this time.

stories.headline: King’s Lynn runner completes ultra marathon for school garden project
stories.brief:
A King’s Lynn man has raised £370 to help restore a sensory garden at Flitcham Primary Academy. John Costin completed the 35-mile Fields and Forests ultra marathon last Saturday, finishing the course through the Suffolk countryside and Thetford Forest in six hours and 38 minutes. 

The funds will support the Friends of Flitcham Primary Academy in renovating the school’s garden, which has been in use for seven years. Mr. Costin launched the fundraiser to assist the school, which has 45 pupils, noting that small rural schools often face funding challenges. Donations for the project are still being accepted via his online fundraising page.

stories.headline: Peterborough United to face Colchester United in EFL Trophy
stories.brief: Peterborough United are set to play Colchester United in the EFL Trophy. Ahead of the upcoming fixture, statistics and head-to-head records for both clubs have been released. Fans looking for information on the match-up can review the latest data regarding the two sides as they prepare for the competition.

stories.headline: Cast revealed for upcoming Ely pantomime
stories.brief: The cast has been introduced for the latest pantomime production taking place in Ely. Organisers are promoting the show as a family-friendly event for the local community. Further details regarding the performance schedule and ticket information can be found via the Ely Standard.

stories.headline: New hydrostat tower installed at Princes food factory
stories.brief: A new hydrostat tower has been installed at the Princes ambient food factory. The facility, which represents an eighty-million-pound investment, is now equipped with the new technology. No further details regarding the installation or the factory's operations have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Police appeal following fatal A10 collision
stories.brief: Cambridgeshire Police are appealing for information following a fatal road traffic collision on the A10. A driver from the Fens has died as a result of the crash. Officers are currently investigating the circumstances surrounding the incident and are urging anyone who may have witnessed the collision or who has relevant dashcam footage to come forward. Further details regarding the exact location and time of the incident have not yet been released by authorities. Anyone with information is encouraged to contact the police to assist with their ongoing enquiries.

stories.headline: Wisbech flats refurbished following council intervention
stories.brief:
Seven flats in Wisbech have been renovated and are now occupied after Fenland District Council intervened to address poor living conditions. The properties, which previously suffered from significant damp and mould, were sold to a new landlord who completed the necessary refurbishments. 

Council officials became involved after a tenant requested support, leading to the identification of the substandard housing. Fenland District Council is now encouraging residents living in poor conditions to come forward for assistance. The local authority investigates approximately 250 private rental properties annually and provides guidance to landlords regarding their legal obligations. Anyone concerned about their housing situation or aware of empty properties is urged to contact the council via their website.

stories.headline: Funding boost for historic King’s Lynn library restoration
stories.brief:
A major restoration project for the former Carnegie library in King’s Lynn has received a significant financial boost. The Workshop, which currently occupies the building, has secured a £249,000 grant from The National Lottery Heritage Fund. 

This funding will support the first phase of capital works, focusing on essential repairs to the roof, chimneys, windows, and the building’s historic parquet flooring. The project aims to preserve the site’s architectural character while improving energy efficiency. The Garage Trust, which operates the venue, intends to transform the landmark into a cultural hub for the community. Further investment has been provided by several other charitable trusts and individual donors to help secure the building's future as an arts centre.

stories.headline: Planning permission refused for listed building conversion
stories.brief: Plans to convert a listed building into a House in Multiple Occupation and a bedsit have been rejected. According to the Spalding South Holland News, the proposal for the site did not receive approval from local planning authorities. No further details regarding the location or the reasons for the refusal have been provided at this time.

stories.headline: Police search for Cambridgeshire man
stories.brief: Cambridgeshire Police are currently searching for a man wanted in connection with a series of serious domestic assaults. Officers are appealing for information regarding his whereabouts. Anyone who may have seen him or who has relevant information is urged to contact the authorities.

stories.headline: Professional flautist visits Gaywood Primary School
stories.brief:
Pupils at Gaywood Primary School have enjoyed a special performance by professional flautist Yu-Wei Lu. The musician, who has performed at the Royal Albert Hall and the Palace of Versailles, visited the school to demonstrate various flutes and share stories from her career. 

Organised by the charity Classical Music Rocks, the event allowed children from Reception to Key Stage 2 to hear live music and learn about different instruments. Music lead Eden Bloomfield said the visit provided a unique opportunity for students to experience classical music firsthand. The charity aims to introduce the genre to primary schools across Norfolk and Suffolk, having reached over 65,000 children since 2016.

stories.headline: Improvements planned for Spalding site
stories.brief: A derelict site in Spalding is set for a transformation. According to reports from the Spalding South Holland News, the area is undergoing a refurbishment to provide a brighter look for the town. No further details regarding the specific location or the nature of the development have been confirmed at this time.

stories.headline: Questions raised over March regeneration project
stories.brief: Fenland District Council is facing new inquiries regarding a one-point-one-two million pound regeneration scheme in March. The project has encountered difficulties following the discovery of a hidden wall during the demolition of the former Barclays bank building. The unexpected find has caused disruption at the site, leading to concerns over the management of the council-led investment. Local officials have yet to provide further details on how this discovery will impact the overall timeline or budget of the redevelopment work.

stories.headline: Cleaning award for HMP Peterborough
stories.brief: HMP Peterborough has received a prestigious award for its cleaning standards. The recognition was reported by the publication FMJ, which covers facilities management news. No further details regarding the specific criteria or the nature of the accolade have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Cambridgeshire man sentenced for racist abuse of England footballer
stories.brief: A man from Cambridgeshire has been sentenced after sending abusive and racist messages to an England footballer. The case was reported by the Ely East Cambridgeshire News. No further details regarding the identity of the individual or the specific footballer involved have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Campaigners oppose school leisure centre closure
stories.brief: Campaigners are challenging a decision to close a leisure centre. The facility, which is attached to a school, is set to shut its doors following an announcement described by those opposing the move as a difficult start to the new year. Local residents are now fighting the school's decision to end the service. Further details regarding the timeline for the closure or the specific school involved have not yet been confirmed.

stories.headline: Prison sentence for controlling partner
stories.brief: A violent abuser has been sent to prison for controlling their partner. The case was reported by the Cambs Times. No further details regarding the location or the length of the sentence have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Arthur Rank Hospice seeks public feedback in Wisbech
stories.brief:
The Arthur Rank Hospice charity is hosting a community engagement event in Wisbech this Tuesday to help shape its upcoming five-year strategy. Representatives from the Alan Hudson Centre will be at the Queen Mary Centre from 1.30pm to gather input from patients, families, staff, volunteers, and the wider public. 

The charity is looking for feedback on its current services and suggestions for future improvements. Those unable to attend the session in person can also contribute their views by completing an online survey. The information gathered will be used to determine the organisation's priorities as it plans for the years ahead.

stories.headline: West Norfolk Befriending hosts community coffee morning
stories.brief:
A charity dedicated to reducing isolation held a coffee morning this past Saturday at Freebridge Haven in West Winch. West Norfolk Befriending organised the event, which featured homemade cakes, a raffle, and a tombola, providing an opportunity for older residents to socialise.

The organisation is currently seeking volunteers aged 18 and over to support residents aged 65 and older across West Norfolk. Volunteers are asked to commit to an hour or two each week, with full training provided. Those interested in helping the charity or learning more about their work can call 01553 763500 or visit their website at wnbefriending.org.uk.

stories.headline: Slavery prevention order issued to Lincolnshire car wash owners
stories.brief: The owners of a car wash business in Lincolnshire have been issued with a ten-year slavery and trafficking risk order. The legal measure follows reporting by the Spalding South Holland News. No further details regarding the individuals involved or the specific location of the business have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Concerns raised over Cambridgeshire SEND school plans
stories.brief: Families across Cambridgeshire are expressing concern following reports of uncertainty surrounding plans for new special educational needs and disabilities schools. According to the BBC, the current situation regarding the proposed SEND school projects is causing worry for those who rely on these services. No further details have been confirmed regarding the specific locations or the timeline for these developments. We will continue to monitor the situation as more information becomes available for residents across the Fens.

stories.headline: Recent cases heard at King’s Lynn Magistrates’ Court
stories.brief:
King’s Lynn Magistrates’ Court has dealt with a series of cases over the past week. Among those appearing was Carl Crawford, 38, of Walton Highway, who admitted to stealing over £5,000 from an elderly woman with Alzheimer’s disease. He will be sentenced at Norwich Crown Court at a later date. 

Meanwhile, 51-year-old Mark Pleasants of Terrington St Clement is due for sentencing on November 5 after admitting to possessing indecent images of children and extreme images depicting rape. Additionally, 32-year-old Olegs Belokurovs was fined £320 for shoplifting trainers from a King’s Lynn store, while 38-year-old Scott Manning received a six-week prison sentence for theft and criminal damage. Other hearings included charges of stalking, drug possession, and assault.

stories.headline: Peterborough City Council announces new SEND strategy
stories.brief: Peterborough City Council has unveiled a new strategy focused on special educational needs and disabilities, known as SEND. The local authority has committed two point one seven million pounds to support the initiative. The funding is intended to improve services for children and young people across the area who have additional educational requirements. Further details regarding the implementation of the plan are expected to follow as the council begins its work on the project.

stories.headline: Man jailed for 22 years for rape offences
stories.brief: A man has been sentenced to 22 years in prison after being convicted of raping a teenager. The sentencing follows an investigation by Cambridgeshire Constabulary into the exploitation of the victim. The force confirmed the outcome of the case, which resulted in the lengthy custodial term for the offender.

stories.headline: Concerns raised over damp and mould at local school
stories.brief: Parents are calling for urgent action regarding the condition of a school building in the region. Reports indicate that concerns have been raised about damp and mould issues within the premises, with claims that the environment is negatively impacting the health of pupils. Those involved are now pressing for improvements to be made to the school facilities.

stories.headline: Sixteen road closures scheduled across Cambridgeshire this week
stories.brief: Motorists travelling across Cambridgeshire are being advised to plan their journeys carefully over the coming days. A total of sixteen road closures are currently in place throughout the county this week. Drivers are encouraged to check local travel updates before setting off to avoid potential delays caused by these works.

stories.headline: New planning applications submitted across West Norfolk
stories.brief:
A range of new planning applications have been submitted to local councils across the region. Among the proposals is a plan to convert the former care home at Adrian Lodge on Gaywood Road in King’s Lynn into a 14-bedroom house of multiple occupation. In Hilgay, an application has been lodged for the installation of three additional holiday pods at the River Meadow Retreat on Hubbards Drove. 

Other notable submissions include a proposal to transform agricultural buildings at Black Drove into three two-bedroom homes, and plans for a new funeral director’s premises on Bexwell Road. Residents can view the full list of planning applications through their local council’s planning portal.

stories.headline: Changes to opening hours at local leisure centre
stories.brief: Residents in the Spalding area are being advised of upcoming changes to the opening hours at their local leisure centre. While the facility will remain open for public use, the times available for visitors are set to be adjusted. Further details regarding the specific new schedule have not yet been confirmed. Those who use the centre regularly are encouraged to check for updates on the revised operating times before planning their next visit.

stories.headline: Man jailed for grooming offence in Cambridgeshire
stories.brief: A man has been sentenced to prison following a grooming offence involving a teenage boy. Cambridgeshire Constabulary confirmed the conviction, which follows an investigation into the incident. No further details regarding the identity of the individual or the specific location of the crime have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Police seize illegal motorbikes in King’s Lynn and West Winch
stories.brief:
West Norfolk Police have seized two petrol-powered motocross bikes following reports of anti-social behaviour. On Wednesday evening, officers confiscated a small green bike in North Lynn after a five-year-old was seen riding it on public roads. A second bike was also recovered in West Winch. 

Police confirmed that both vehicles had been illegally modified and were not permitted for road use. Officers have expressed concern regarding the dangerous use of these bikes on footpaths and shared spaces. Residents are being urged to report information about where these vehicles are stored and who is operating them to assist with ongoing investigations.

stories.headline: Peterborough United to face Colchester United
stories.brief: Peterborough United are set to play Colchester United in an upcoming football fixture. The match, titled On the Road with the U's, sees the Peterborough side travelling to compete against their opponents. Fans are advised to keep an eye on local sports schedules for further details regarding the kick-off time and venue arrangements for this encounter.

stories.headline: Ely school told to improve by Ofsted
stories.brief: An Ely school has been told it must urgently improve following a recent inspection by Ofsted. The school has expressed disappointment regarding the findings of the education watchdog. No further details have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Long Sutton father and son sentenced for Christmas Day assault
stories.brief: A father and son from Long Sutton have avoided prison sentences following an assault that took place on Christmas Day. The pair appeared in court regarding the incident, which occurred during the festive period. Both men were spared immediate jail time for their roles in the attack.

stories.headline: Cambridgeshire jewellers close branch following break-ins
stories.brief: A Cambridgeshire jewellery business has announced the closure of one of its branches. The decision follows two separate break-ins at the premises within the current year. The store will no longer operate at the affected location.

stories.headline: King’s Lynn Rotarians raise funds for Nepal flood victims
stories.brief:
Members of the King’s Lynn Priory Rotary Club have raised thousands of pounds to support those affected by recent flash floods in Nepal. Following the disaster, which was triggered by a collapsing glacier, club member John Harrison launched a fundraising drive to provide emergency shelter boxes. These kits contain essential supplies, including bedding, cooking equipment, and shelter for families who have lost their homes.

So far, the group has collected £3,000, enough to fund five shelter boxes. Additionally, the club has donated £500 to the Rotary District’s Nepal Disaster Appeal. Mr. Harrison, who previously served in the Royal Air Force, has a long-standing personal connection to the region through his past trekking and climbing expeditions.

stories.headline: New cafe opens in Spalding
stories.brief: A new cafe has opened its doors in Spalding. The business has been launched by a duo, according to reports from the Spalding South Holland News. No further details regarding the location or the name of the establishment have been provided at this time.

stories.headline: March Rugby Club faces pressure from town expansion
stories.brief: A rugby club in March has reported that it is operating beyond its capacity. The organisation says the situation has been caused by the unprecedented growth of the market town. The club is currently struggling to manage the increased demand placed upon its facilities.

stories.headline: Dersingham charity event raises over £15,000 for Queen Elizabeth Hospital
stories.brief:
A fundraising event in Dersingham has raised more than £15,000 to support breast care and cancer services at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn. The inaugural "Breastfest," organised by the charity Breast of Friends, was held at The Pastures behind the Coach and Horses. 

The event featured live music, entertainment, and food, with the final total reaching £15,192.78. Charity trustees thanked the volunteers, performers, and local business sponsors who contributed to the day's success. The funds will assist the charity in its ongoing work to improve patient care and provide support kits for those receiving treatment at the hospital.

stories.headline: Positive results in gene therapy trial for rare eye condition
stories.brief: A gene therapy treatment developed by Beacon has reached a primary goal during a clinical trial for a rare eye disease. According to the Peterborough Fenland Edge News, the study marks a significant milestone for the medical research project. Further details regarding the specific nature of the condition or the trial's next steps have not yet been released.

stories.headline: MP calls for NHS dental reform in East Cambridgeshire
stories.brief: The local MP for Ely and East Cambridgeshire is calling for urgent NHS reforms, describing the area as a "dental desert." The Member of Parliament is highlighting significant concerns regarding access to dental services for residents across the region. The call for change comes as part of a wider push for improvements to the current healthcare system.

stories.headline: March business reaches national kitchen award final
stories.brief: A family-run business based in March has been named as a finalist for a national kitchen renovation award. The company, which operates locally, is now in the running for the industry accolade. No further details regarding the specific award or the date of the final ceremony have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Senior doctors warn of workforce crisis at Queen Elizabeth Hospital
stories.brief:
Senior medics at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn have warned that potential plans to downgrade A&E, intensive care, and maternity services could trigger a severe workforce crisis. In a leaked letter, consultants expressed profound concern that ongoing uncertainty is already damaging staff recruitment and retention. 

The Norfolk and Waveney University Hospitals Group, which is reviewing clinical services, maintains that no decisions have been made regarding the future of these units. However, clinicians argue that a lack of clear refutation is undermining public confidence. The hospital serves a wide rural area, including parts of North Cambridgeshire and South Lincolnshire, leading to fears that any reduction in services would pose a significant risk to patient safety.

stories.headline: Wisbech man jailed for shoplifting offences
stories.brief:
A 44-year-old man from Wisbech has been sentenced to 13 months in prison for a series of shoplifting offences. Lee Thompson, of John F Kennedy Court, targeted the Tesco Express on Kirkgate Street three times between August 14 and 18. He also admitted to stealing from the Boots store in the Horsefair Shopping Centre back in May, alongside further offences committed in Norfolk.

Following his arrest by neighbourhood officers, Thompson appeared at Huntingdon Magistrates’ Court last Tuesday. The sentence includes the activation of previous suspended terms. In addition to his jail time, Thompson has been ordered to pay £99.99 in compensation. Police have thanked members of the public for reporting retail crime, noting that such information is vital for identifying offenders.

stories.headline: Norfolk County Council seeks feedback on recycling centres
stories.brief:
Norfolk County Council is inviting residents to share their views on the county’s 19 recycling centres. An annual satisfaction survey is now open, covering sites including those in King’s Lynn, Wereham, Docking, Heacham, and Ashill. 

The council says the feedback will help identify potential service improvements and understand any barriers to usage. Last year, the centres processed nearly 56,000 tonnes of household waste, with over 75 per cent diverted from general disposal. Residents can complete the short questionnaire online until October 18. Further details and the survey link are available on the Norfolk County Council website.

stories.headline: Cambridgeshire charity faces funding gap for LGBTQ+ youth services
stories.brief: A Cambridgeshire charity is warning that its services for LGBTQ+ young people are currently at risk. The organisation has reported a significant funding shortfall, which threatens the future of the support it provides across the region. Further details regarding the specific impact on local programmes have not yet been confirmed.

stories.headline: Long Sutton travel agents support Santa appeal
stories.brief: Staff at a travel agency in Long Sutton have been busy preparing for the festive season. The team at the local branch have been packing a suitcase for Santa Claus as part of a seasonal initiative. The project aims to support the community during the upcoming holidays.

stories.headline: Man charged following jewellery shop break-in
stories.brief: A man has been charged after a jewellery shop was broken into. This incident marks the second time the business has been targeted in less than a year. Police have confirmed the charge following the break-in.

stories.headline: Inquest concludes into fatal Wisbech crash
stories.brief:
An inquest has heard that 18-year-old Declan Berry was driving at 90mph before his car crashed into a river in Wisbech. The hearing at Cambridgeshire Coroners Court was told the vehicle, which was carrying five teenagers, hit a pothole on North Brink on March 18 before rolling into the water. 

Three passengers escaped the submerged car with help from a local resident, but Mr Berry and another passenger died in the incident. Coroner Elizabeth Grey concluded that excessive speed was the primary cause of the collision, while noting that the poor condition of the road was a contributing factor. The court heard that the local council had previously received over 100 complaints regarding the state of the road.

stories.headline: Residents raise concerns over road conditions in March
stories.brief: People living in March have described the state of a local road as being like a war zone due to the number of potholes. Residents have expressed their frustration regarding the poor condition of the surface. The reports were highlighted by the BBC.

stories.headline: News update: QEH rebuild delay, Swaffham car park transfer and local business news
stories.brief:
The Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn faces a further delay to its rebuild project, with the completion date now pushed back to 2033. Hospital leadership has confirmed that while 24-hour emergency care will continue, the potential closure of the current A&E department has not been ruled out.

In other local news, Swaffham Town Council has taken ownership of the Theatre Street and Lynn Street car parks from Breckland Council. Meanwhile, in Middleton, the former Middletons Steak House has reopened as The Middleton Crown following a major refurbishment. Finally, a new mobile mechanics service has been launched to support residents across West Norfolk, including those in the Downham, Swaffham, and Wisbech areas.

stories.headline: Hundreds of heritage assets identified in East Cambridgeshire
stories.brief: A total of 678 local heritage assets have been identified across East Cambridgeshire. The findings were reported by the Ely East Cambridgeshire News. These sites have now been officially recognised as part of the region's heritage.

stories.headline: Police praise victim after predator conviction
stories.brief: Lincolnshire Police have commended the bravery of a victim who was targeted by an offender starting from the age of eleven. Officers described the perpetrator as an abhorrent predator following the conclusion of the case. The force highlighted the courage shown by the individual in coming forward to report the abuse.

stories.headline: Council rejects new crossing for March school
stories.brief: Parents in March have expressed frustration after the local council turned down a request for a new pedestrian crossing near a school. The decision has sparked anger among families who were calling for improved safety measures in the area. The March Chatteris Whittlesey News reports that the proposal was formally rejected by the council. No further details regarding the specific location or the council's reasoning for the refusal have been provided at this time.
